item.meaning: The continuous geological landmass combining Europe and Asia without a surrounding ocean barrier.
A body of land entirely surrounded by water on all sides, such as Greenland or Sri Lanka.
A series of immense ocean waves generated by underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides.

item.title: Oceans as Global Life Support Systems
item.explanation: Oceans cover ~71% of Earth, drive the water cycle via evaporation and rainfall, and produce over 50% of atmospheric oxygen through marine phytoplankton.

item.statement: Water covers approximately 71% of Earth's surface, while land covers about 29%.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean, covering more area than all continental landmasses combined.
Greenland is the largest island on Earth.

item.name: Greenland
item.significance: The world's largest island, located in the North Atlantic / Arctic Ocean.

item.name: Lakshadweep
item.significance: India's coral island union territory located in the Arabian Sea.

item.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
item.significance: India's volcanic island union territory situated in the Bay of Bengal.

item.historical_significance: A devastating tsunami triggered by a massive underwater earthquake off Sumatra, Indonesia, affecting coastal India and lead to the creation of NDMA.

item.description: The Earth's largest and deepest ocean, covering more than 30% of the globe.
